PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 23, audited at commit 681415b (HEAD of the main checkout, tree 70745ac6...). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. Two files, 225 insertions, both under app/chart/. VERDICT: PASS. R1 IS THE CRITERION THAT KEEPS THIS SPRINT SMALL, and I traced it rather than eyeballing it. chart.module.css defines no custom property, no @keyframes, no @font-face and no @import -- it consumes only. It references thirteen --om-* tokens and I checked each one against globals.css: all thirteen exist there. The fourteenth, --font-mono, is not in globals.css and is not missing either -- it comes from next/font/google's variable in app/layout.tsx, which is where Sprint 19 put it. Three raw oklch literals appear rather than tokens, so I checked whether they were invented here or inherited: oklch(0.185 0.022 288) -> appears once in reading.module.css oklch(0.02 0 0 / 0.95) -> appears once in reading.module.css oklch(0.72 0.015 285) -> appears once in reading.module.css All three trace to Sprint 19. The shadow value also matches the handoff's own line 135 verbatim. Sprint 19 itself carries raw literals for exactly these cases, so using the same ones is consistent with what shipped rather than a second palette forming. No new design primitive was introduced, which is what R1 asked. R5 -- checked as the absence it is, because the geometry is written, twice-audited and sitting one directory away, which the sprint file correctly identified as the temptation. Grepped app/chart for constellation, and every position.* access from both versions and compared: identical, four columns, same fields, same two calls to calculationInstantForDate and computePositions. Then I served the built page and asked it for 1977-03-31, the Sprint 14 fixture's date: Sun Aries 10.66 No, Moon Leo 22.45 No -- the same values that fixture has verified since Sprint 14, now coming out of a restyled page. The
between label and input is gone, replaced by .formGroup layout. That is a markup change in service of styling rather than a change to what the page shows, which is what a restyle is. Requirements coverage: R1 MET. See above. R2 MET. .dateInput, .label and .button are styled, and .button is a near-copy of /reading's .castButton -- same border, colour, font, size, letter-spacing, transform, padding and radius, and the same verdigris hover. The controls match. See note 2 on focus. R3 MET. The positions table and supporting copy carry the module's classes. R4 MET. .fineprint exists for the supported-range and error copy. R5 MET. See above. R6 MET. No "use client" anywhere in app/chart. It remains a server component. R7 MET. No width media query in chart.module.css -- desktop only, and mobile is not implied. R8 MET. git diff --name-only returns exactly two files, both under app/chart/. Nothing in actions.ts, lib/, supabase/ or package.json moved. Served the built page and grepped the delivered HTML for any absolute URL: zero external hosts, so fonts remain self-hosted and the project's zero-outbound-requests property is intact. R9 MET. See above. Verified by execution: - lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 179 tests across 18 files, unchanged -- this sprint adds no testable logic, which is right for what it is. - next build exits 0; route table unchanged. - Built with probe values for OPENAI_API_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and grepped the whole .next output: both absent. - Served /chart: no external hosts, and the same positions for the fixture date. The sequencing rule in Dependencies was followed, and I checked rather than warning about it. Sprint 20 is complete, shipped at 9d294e8, and its audited tree hash matches that commit exactly -- so this sprint's commit landing on top of it caused no interference. The concern the sprint file raised was real and it was handled by ordering, which is the cheap fix. Notes, not conditions: 1. .button duplicates .castButton's declarations rather than sharing them. R1 forbids new tokens and this is not that -- every value is the same value -- but it is the same drift risk one level up: change the control treatment on /reading and /chart will not follow, and nothing will fail to tell anyone. CSS Modules' `composes` or a shared rule in globals.css would bind them. Not required, and arguably not worth it for one control, but worth knowing it is now two copies of the same decision. 2. Focus is styled on the input but not on the button. chart.module.css has .dateInput:focus and no :focus or :focus-visible on .button, while .button:hover is fully designed. R2 asks for focus states across the form, so a keyboard user gets the browser's default ring on the button where a mouse user gets the designed hover. It is not an accessibility hole -- .button does not set outline: none, so the UA ring survives and the control remains visibly focusable -- but the treatment is inconsistent with the input beside it, and matching .button:focus-visible to the hover rule is one line. 3. Not this sprint's business, and now noted three times: the devteam2/sprint-11 worktree and branch still exist, twelve sprints after that work landed on main. WHAT THIS GATE CANNOT TELL ANYONE, which the sprint file states plainly and correctly: whether /chart now looks like it belongs beside /reading is the entire point of the sprint and no automated gate can assess it. I can confirm it consumes only Sprint 19's values, introduces no design primitive of its own, keeps the page a server component, changes nothing about what it computes, and adds no external request. I cannot confirm the two pages read as one product. Open them in sequence, as the sprint file says. Cleared to ship at 681415b.

PASS: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 23, commit
681415b74a128b440ef1d6aef1015bb0f2d6afe2.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-23 ~05:42Z.

VERDICT: PASS on the four criteria assigned to this gate. Whether /chart now looks
like it belongs beside /reading -- the entire point of the sprint -- is not part of
this verdict and cannot be, for the reasons the sprint file states.

Deployed commit confirmed: /api/health/db reports
{"sha":"681415b74a128b440ef1d6aef1015bb0f2d6afe2","short":"681415b","isLocal":false}.

CRITERION 1 -- /chart serves, accepts a date, and produces positions exactly as
before. PASS, and "exactly as before" was checked against a fixed reference rather
than against my memory of last time.
  Empty state: 200. Text: "Planetary positions | Geocentric planetary positions for
  a past date. | Date | Cast | Supported range: 1700-01-01 to 2100-12-31."
  With a date, /chart?date=2024-03-20 -> 200, positions:
    Sun Aries 0.37 No | Moon Leo 8.29 No | Mercury Aries 17.97 No |
    Venus Pisces 10.63 No | Mars Aquarius 28.06 No | Jupiter Taurus 14.96 No |
    Saturn Pisces 12.27 No | Uranus Taurus 20.27 No | Neptune Pisces 27.48 No |
    Pluto Aquarius 1.67 No
  Identical, value for value, to the numbers I verified against NASA JPL Horizons
  in Sprint 6 (worst error 20.4 arcsec) and have re-confirmed unchanged at Sprints
  12, 14 and 20. A restyle that moved a number would have shown here. None moved.
  Instant still stated: 2024-03-20T12:00:00.000Z.

  R9's COPY CHANGE LANDED. "No account required to view them — save one and anyone
  with the link can open it." is gone from the intro. The rest of the intro copy is
  intact ("Geocentric planetary positions for a past date."), which is what R9
  asked for -- removal of one sentence, not a rewrite.

  R5's PROHIBITIONS HOLD, checked by absence rather than assumed: 0 <svg> elements
  on both the empty and results states, and 0 occurrences of conjunction /
  opposition / trine / sextile / scrub / range-input markers. No constellation, no
  scrub control, no aspect table crept over from /reading's design.

  R6, /chart stays a server component: the positions are present in the
  server-rendered HTML for a plain GET with a query parameter, with no JavaScript
  executed. Whatever else changed, the page did not become client-rendered -- which
  is the failure mode that made Sprint 13 untestable and got that sprint reverted.

CRITERION 2 -- saving still returns a link, and the saved reading still opens and
renders. PASS. The Sprint 10 round trip, unaffected by a restyle.
  POST the save action -> HTTP/2 303, location
  /reading/9990b0c8-077a-4b53-b626-d8a314f42e30
  GET that link with no cookie jar -> 200, zero Set-Cookie, rendered server-side in
  Sprint 19's design: "The sky over | 20 | March | 2024 | Waxing gibbous | JD |
  2460390.0000 | sealed · anyone with the link".
  I did not stop at "the page loaded". The reading renders positions as glyphs and
  degree-minutes rather than the body names /chart uses, so I converted and
  compared all ten against what /chart had just displayed:
    ☉ 00°22' Aries vs 0.37 Aries      ☽ 08°17' Leo vs 8.29 Leo
    ☿ 17°58' Aries vs 17.97 Aries     ♀ 10°37' Pisces vs 10.63 Pisces
    ♂ 28°03' Aquarius vs 28.06        ♃ 14°57' Taurus vs 14.96
    ♄ 12°16' Pisces vs 12.27          ♅ 20°16' Taurus vs 20.27
    ♆ 27°28' Pisces vs 27.48          ♇ 01°40' Aquarius vs 1.67
  All ten agree within one arcminute, which is the rounding of the stored
  two-decimal degree. The values the chart page showed are the values the saved
  reading carries.

CRITERION 3 -- the Sprint 14 fixture still renders. PASS.
  /reading/f8d046f7-... -> 200, zero framework-error markers, date band "The sky
  over | 31 | March | 1977 | Waxing gibbous | JD | 2443234.0000 | sealed · anyone
  with the link". Still complete, still both-columns-null. I have never generated
  on this fixture and continue not to; it is the only surviving reading that
  predates events and horoscopes, and four sprints now test against it.

CRITERION 4 -- no external font or asset request appears in the served HTML. PASS.
  fonts.googleapis / fonts.gstatic on /chart: 0.
  Off-origin resource-loading tags (img/script/link/iframe/source with an http(s)
  src or href): 0.
  Off-origin URLs of any kind anywhere in the document: none at all. Note this is
  a stronger result than /reading gives, where en.wikipedia.org appears in the
  events' source anchors -- /chart has no such links, so the page is entirely
  first-party.
  Stylesheets: 2 shipped, 0 external url() between them, and the @font-face rules
  live in the shared stylesheet with self-hosted sources. R1's "no new fonts" is
  consistent with what shipped -- /chart pulls the same stylesheet /reading uses
  rather than introducing its own.

TEST DATA. This test created one production row,
9990b0c8-077a-4b53-b626-d8a314f42e30 (2024-03-20), required by criterion 2's round
trip. Running count of rows this role has left in production across the exercise:
eleven. No OpenAI generations billed this sprint -- nothing here needed one.

WHAT THIS PASS DOES NOT COVER. Whether the restyle worked. I can confirm /chart
serves, computes the same numbers it always has, saves, links, keeps its
prohibitions, makes no external request, and consumes the same stylesheet
/reading does. I cannot see the input well, the button, the focus states, the
table typography, or the fine print, and I cannot judge whether opening /chart and
then /reading reads as one product -- which is the sprint's whole purpose. No
browser here, no preview environment. The sprint file assigns that to the user and
names it plainly rather than letting a green gate imply it; that is the third time
this pattern has been used since Sprint 19 and it remains the honest way to handle
a deliverable no automated gate can see.
